entities.name: Amebiasis
entities.description: Invasive protozoan infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica, manifesting as amoebic colitis and extraintestinal amoebic liver abscess.

entities.name: Amoebic dysentery
entities.description: Invasive intestinal protozoan syndrome characterized by frequent mucoid and bloody stools accompanied by lower abdominal cramps.

entities.name: Currant jelly stool
entities.description: Passage of dark maroon altered blood and mucus intimately mixed with feces, pathognomonic of subacute amoebic colitis.

entities.name: Subacute crampy abdominal pain
entities.description: Progressive lower abdominal colicky discomfort evolving insidiously over one to three weeks.

entities.name: Tenesmus
entities.description: Painful and distressing sensation of urgent, incomplete rectal evacuation resulting from rectal ulceration.

entities.name: Uncomplicated amoebic colitis
entities.description: Subacute non-toxic intestinal infection with moderate diarrhea, weight loss, and localized abdominal tenderness.

entities.name: Absent fever in colitis
entities.description: Paradoxical lack of significant pyrexia occurring in 60% to 80% of uncomplicated amoebic dysentery cases.

entities.name: Fulminant necrotizing colitis
entities.description: Severe transmural colonic necrosis and gangrene accompanied by extreme toxicity, fever, and peritonitis.

entities.name: Toxic megacolon
entities.description: Non-obstructive rapid segmental or total colonic dilation complicated by impending perforation, often exacerbated by steroids.

entities.name: Colonic perforation
entities.description: Transmural breach of ulcerated colon leading to acute feculent peritonitis, hemodynamic collapse, and high mortality.

entities.name: Amoeboma
entities.description: Exophytic chronic inflammatory pseudotumoral mass of granulation tissue in the colon, most often cecal.

entities.name: Colonic stricture
entities.description: Fibrotic luminal narrowing of the large intestine occurring as a late sequel to transmural amoebic ulceration.

entities.name: Chronic amoebic colitis
entities.description: Protracted relapsing-remitting diarrhea, recurrent abdominal pain, anorexia, and asthenia mimicking Crohn disease.

entities.name: Lower gastrointestinal hemorrhage
entities.description: Substantial or massive rectal bleeding resulting from deep trophozoite erosion into colonic submucosal vessels.

entities.name: Appendiceal amebiasis
entities.description: Invasive trophozoite infection localized to the vermiform appendix mimicking acute bacterial appendicitis.

entities.name: Amoebic liver abscess
entities.description: Most frequent extraintestinal amebiasis manifestation caused by portal venous migration and hepatic liquefactive necrosis.

entities.name: Right upper quadrant pain
entities.description: Constant, dull, aching discomfort in the right hypochondrium accentuated by motion, coughing, or inspiration.

entities.name: Remittent high fever
entities.description: Spiking elevated body temperature between 38.5°C and 40°C accompanied by chills, rigors, and profuse sweats.

entities.name: Drenching night sweats
entities.description: Profound nocturnal diaphoresis associated with cyclic defervescence during extraintestinal hepatic suppuration.

entities.name: Absence of diarrhea
entities.description: Paradoxical clinical absence of concurrent bowel looseness or dysentery in over 70% to 80% of amoebic liver abscess cases.

entities.name: Tender hepatomegaly
entities.description: Enlarged, smooth liver extending several centimeters below the right costal margin with exquisite palpation tenderness.

entities.name: Referred right shoulder pain
entities.description: Phrenic nerve mediated ipsilateral shoulder discomfort arising from diaphragmatic irritation by superior liver abscess.

entities.name: Weight loss and anorexia
entities.description: Profound constitutional wasting, loss of appetite, and asthenia driven by high systemic tumor necrosis factor levels.

entities.name: Amoebic liver rupture
entities.description: Sudden breach of hepatic abscess wall into adjacent peritoneal, pleural, pericardial, or retroperitoneal cavities.

entities.name: Amoebic peritonitis
entities.description: Acute generalized or localized peritoneal inflammation caused by rupture of a subcapsular liver abscess or colonic perforation.

entities.name: Pleuropulmonary amebiasis
entities.description: Thoracic amebiasis resulting from transdiaphragmatic extension, direct cavitation, or sympathetic pleural effusion.

entities.name: Sympathetic pleural effusion
entities.description: Sterile, reactive serous exudate accumulating in the right hemithorax above an active subdiaphragmatic hepatic abscess.

entities.name: Amoebic empyema
entities.description: Direct transdiaphragmatic rupture of an amoebic liver abscess filling the pleural cavity with thick necrotic chocolate fluid.

entities.name: Hepatobronchial fistula
entities.description: Abnormal fistulous tract connecting a liver abscess across the diaphragm directly into a major branch of the bronchial tree.

entities.name: Anchovy sputum expectoration
entities.description: Productive coughing and expectoration of copious thick, reddish-brown necrotic lung fluid via a hepatobronchial fistula.

entities.name: Right lower lobe consolidation
entities.description: Secondary basilar pneumonic consolidation and compressive atelectasis in the right lower lung above a hepatic abscess.

entities.name: Amoebic pericarditis
entities.description: Acute purulent or serous pericardial inflammation resulting from direct transpericardial rupture of a left hepatic lobe abscess.

entities.name: Cardiac tamponade
entities.description: Obstructive hemodynamic collapse caused by acute fluid accumulation of necrotic amoebic material inside the pericardium.

entities.name: Cerebral amebiasis
entities.description: Extremely rare, highly fatal hematogenous central nervous system amebiasis manifesting as necrotic brain abscesses.

entities.name: Cutaneous amebiasis
entities.description: Painful, rapidly progressive destructive necrotizing ulceration of perianal skin, surgical wounds, or genitalia.

entities.name: Amoebic balanitis
entities.description: Painful ulcerative necrotizing inflammation of the glans penis transmitted via direct oro-anal sexual exposure.

entities.name: Genitourinary amebiasis
entities.description: Rare invasive infection of the bladder, urethra, or female genital tract causing ulceration, hematuria, and discharge.

entities.name: Splenic abscess
entities.description: Rare hematogenous abscess localized in splenic parenchyma presenting with left hypochondrial pain and fever.

entities.name: Amoebic typhlitis
entities.description: Severe localized amoebic ulceration and transmural edema isolated to the cecum presenting with right lower quadrant peritonitis.

entities.name: Mild jaundice
entities.description: Low-grade scleral icterus occurring in under 10% of patients with massive solitary or central amoebic liver abscesses.

entities.name: Rigors and chills
entities.description: Episodes of intense shivering accompanied by feeling cold during rapid spikes of core body temperature in hepatic amebiasis.

entities.name: Anchovy-paste aspirate
entities.description: Thick, odorless, reddish-brown chocolate-colored necrotic hepatocyte liquefactive fluid aspirated from cavity.

entities.name: Flask-shaped colonic ulcer
entities.description: Colonic mucosal ulcer with narrow neck and wide lateral submucosal base with undermined margins.

entities.name: Fecal erythrophagocytosis
entities.description: Microscopic demonstration of motile Entamoeba trophozoites containing ingested host red blood cells.

entities.name: Odorless liver pus
entities.description: Absence of foul, putrid odor in freshly aspirated amoebic abscess fluid, reflecting sterile hepatic tissue necrosis.

entities.name: Hepatobronchial fistulization
entities.description: Direct clinical expectoration of chocolate necrotic liver fluid across a ruptured diaphragmatic bronchial channel.

entities.name: Normal intervening colonic mucosa
entities.description: Discrete focal mucosal ulcerations interspersed with completely uninvolved, healthy mucosal surfaces.

entities.name: Trophozoites in ulcer margin
entities.description: Viable amebic trophozoites localized strictly at the advancing outer rim of the lesion rather than necrotic center.

entities.name: Amoeboma pseudotumor
entities.description: Firm granulomatous inflammatory pseudotumor that dramatically melts and resolves following nitroimidazole therapy.

entities.name: Liver Murphy sign
entities.description: Inspiratory arrest or sharp pain paroxysm elicited by palpation or intercostal percussion of the liver edge.

entities.name: Intercostal point tenderness
entities.description: Focal exquisite pain elicited by one-finger palpation over the right 8th to 10th intercostal spaces in the midaxillary line.

entities.name: Smooth tender hepatomegaly
entities.description: Uniformly smooth, tender liver edge palpable 2 to 5 cm below the right costal margin.

entities.name: Right lower rib punch
entities.description: Sharp pain paroxysm elicited by gentle fist percussion over the right lower thoracic rib cage.

entities.name: Right lung base dullness
entities.description: Percussion dullness at the posterior right hemithorax base from elevated diaphragm and sympathetic pleural effusion.

entities.name: Decreased breath sounds right
entities.description: Diminished or absent vesicular breath sounds at the right lung base over an elevated diaphragm and effusion.

entities.name: Right upper quadrant guarding
entities.description: Involuntary muscular defense and resistance palpated over the right hypochondrium.

entities.name: Palpable right iliac mass
entities.description: Firm, tender, fixed or mobile mass palpated in the right lower abdominal quadrant corresponding to cecal amoeboma.

entities.name: Abdominal distension
entities.description: Visible symmetric or asymmetric abdominal expansion and tympany from paralytic ileus or toxic megacolon.

entities.name: Involuntary abdominal rigidity
entities.description: Board-like involuntary abdominal wall spasm indicating acute peritonitis from perforation or abscess rupture.

entities.name: Hypoactive bowel sounds
entities.description: Marked diminution or absence of peristaltic sounds on abdominal auscultation due to peritonitis or toxic colitis.

entities.name: Localized rebound tenderness
entities.description: Sharp pain upon rapid release of palpation pressure (Blumberg sign) over inflamed colonic or hepatic serosa.

entities.name: Tender rectosigmoid on DRE
entities.description: Severe pain elicited during digital rectal examination with dark blood and mucus detected on examining glove.

entities.name: Scleral icterus
entities.description: Yellow discoloration of the sclerae detectable in approximately 5% to 10% of patients with extensive liver abscesses.

entities.name: Fever above 39C
entities.description: High core temperature exceeding 39.0°C measured during acute presentation of extraintestinal amoebic liver abscess.

entities.name: Tachycardia out of proportion
entities.description: Disproportionate resting heart rate elevation driven by systemic inflammatory mediators and intravascular depletion.

entities.name: Focal chest wall bulge
entities.description: Visible localized intercostal fullness, edema, or erythema overlying an expanding subcapsular right lobe abscess.

entities.name: Pericardial friction rub
entities.description: Superficial, scratching high-pitched precordial sound auscultated during contiguous left lobe pericardial involvement.

entities.name: Pulsus paradoxus
entities.description: Exaggerated inspiratory systolic blood pressure decline exceeding 10 mmHg caused by amoebic tamponade.

entities.name: Indurated cutaneous ulcer margins
entities.description: Elevated, violaceous, deeply undermined borders surrounding painful necrotic ulcers in cutaneous amebiasis.

entities.name: Neutrophilic leukocytosis
entities.description: Elevated peripheral white blood cell count (12,000 to 25,000/mcL) with prominent neutrophilia in >80% of ALA.

entities.name: Left shift bandemia
entities.description: Presence of greater than 10% immature band forms on peripheral blood smear reflecting acute systemic inflammation.

entities.name: Absence of eosinophilia
entities.description: Normal absolute eosinophil count and normal percentage (<3%), differentiating protozoan infection from helminths.

entities.name: Normocytic normochromic anemia
entities.description: Mild to moderate reduction in hemoglobin with normal red cell indices due to acute and chronic inflammation.

entities.name: Elevated alkaline phosphatase
entities.description: Serum ALP elevation 2 to 4 times the upper limit of normal observed in 75% to 80% of amoebic liver abscess cases.

entities.name: Mild transaminitis
entities.description: Mild to moderate serum AST and ALT elevations (1.5 to 3 times upper limit of normal) reflecting hepatocyte necrosis.

entities.name: Normal serum bilirubin
entities.description: Total serum bilirubin within normal reference range or only minimally elevated (<2 to 3 mg/dL).

entities.name: Hypoalbuminemia
entities.description: Serum albumin depression (<3.0 g/dL) secondary to negative acute-phase response and systemic catabolism.

entities.name: Markedly elevated CRP
entities.description: Serum C-reactive protein concentrations markedly elevated above 100 to 200 mg/L.

entities.name: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
entities.description: Significantly accelerated ESR exceeding 60 to 100 mm/hour during acute extraintestinal infection.

entities.name: Positive serum amoebic serology
entities.description: Serum anti-amoebic IgG antibodies detected via ELISA or indirect hemagglutination with >95% sensitivity after day 7.

entities.name: Fecal Gal-GalNAc lectin antigen
entities.description: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent detection of Entamoeba histolytica Gal/GalNAc adherence lectin in stool specimens.

entities.name: Real-time fecal PCR
entities.description: Molecular DNA amplification targeting 18S ribosomal RNA of Entamoeba histolytica in fecal samples.

entities.name: Motile stool trophozoites
entities.description: Direct microscopic observation of live 15 to 40 micrometer amoebic trophozoites with progressive pseudopodial motion.

entities.name: Aspirate amoebic PCR
entities.description: Polymerase chain reaction detecting E. histolytica DNA in liver abscess fluid or biopsy material.

entities.name: Aspirate Gal-GalNAc lectin ELISA
entities.description: Antigen immunoassay detecting amebic adherence lectin directly in aspirated chocolate abscess fluid.

entities.name: Absence of fecal neutrophils
entities.description: Microscopic stool wet mount showing few or degenerated neutrophils (pyknotic bodies), unlike sheets in bacterial colitis.

entities.name: Microscopic fecal erythrocytes
entities.description: Presence of numerous microscopic red blood cells in diarrheal stool wet mounts without dense neutrophil sheets.

entities.name: Sterile bacterial blood cultures
entities.description: Negative blood cultures for aerobic and anaerobic bacterial organisms during acute hepatic febrile presentation.

entities.name: Sterile aspirate bacterial culture
entities.description: Aspirated chocolate hepatic necrotic fluid demonstrates complete lack of bacterial growth on standard culture media.

entities.name: Solitary hepatic hypoechoic lesion
entities.description: Bedside POCUS demonstrating a single round or oval hypoechoic cavity with low-level internal acoustic echoes in 70-85%.

entities.name: Segment VII-VIII liver lesion
entities.description: Sonographic or CT localization of hepatic abscess cavity predominantly in the posterior-superior segments of the right lobe.

entities.name: Subcapsular liver abutment
entities.description: Immediate proximity and contact of the hypoechoic cavity with the Glisson capsule of the liver on ultrasound.

entities.name: Absence of calcified rim
entities.description: Lack of peripheral dense curvilinear eggshell calcification on ultrasound or plain radiography.

entities.name: Absence of daughter cysts
entities.description: Sonographic cavity demonstrating uniform liquefactive debris without internal septations or daughter vesicles.

entities.name: Posterior acoustic enhancement
entities.description: Increased echo intensity deep to the hepatic lesion on ultrasound reflecting its predominantly fluid liquefactive content.

entities.name: Elevated right hemidiaphragm
entities.description: Chest radiography demonstrating upward displacement and tenting of the right diaphragm above an expanding liver abscess.

entities.name: Blunting of costophrenic angle
entities.description: Radiographic obliteration of the sharp right lateral or posterior costophrenic sulcus by reactive fluid.

entities.name: Right basilar atelectasis
entities.description: Horizontal band-like compression atelectasis in the right lower lung field on chest radiograph.

entities.name: Hypodense CT liver lesion
entities.description: Well-demarcated non-enhancing fluid attenuation cavity (10 to 30 Hounsfield units) on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT.

entities.name: Peripheral enhancing abscess rim
entities.description: Smooth, thin, hypervascular peripheral wall enhancement on late arterial and portal venous phase CT imaging.

entities.name: Edema halo around lesion
entities.description: Zone of low attenuation surrounding the liver abscess wall on CT representing perilesional hepatic parenchymal edema.

entities.name: Pericardial effusion on echocardiography
entities.description: Bedside transthoracic echo demonstrating anechoic pericardial fluid accumulation from a left lobe liver abscess.

entities.name: Subphrenic fluid collection
entities.description: Sonographic or CT detection of fluid pooling in the space between the liver dome and the diaphragm.

entities.name: Pneumoperitoneum on abdominal X-ray
entities.description: Free subdiaphragmatic crescentic air under the diaphragm on upright plain film indicating colonic perforation.

entities.name: Thumbprinting sign on X-ray
entities.description: Scalloped mucosal impressions along the colonic margin on plain abdominal film reflecting severe submucosal edema.

entities.name: Collar-button ulcer on endoscopy
entities.description: Endoscopic identification of discrete mucosal ulcers with narrow necks and undermined borders.

entities.name: Amoeboma cecal mass lesion
entities.description: Exophytic, circumferential luminal narrowing and lobulated mass in the cecum visualized on colonoscopy or barium enema.

entities.name: Chlorine-resistant cyst ingestion
entities.description: Oral consumption of viable quadri-nucleate Entamoeba cysts that survive routine public water chlorination.

entities.name: Contaminated drinking water
entities.description: Ingestion of unboiled or untreated tap or well water contaminated with human fecal waste.

entities.name: Nightsoil-fertilized produce
entities.description: Eating unwashed or raw fruits and vegetables cultivated using untreated human excrement as agricultural fertilizer.

entities.name: Tropical endemic travel
entities.description: Travel or prior residence in tropical and subtropical regions lacking adequate sewage treatment facilities.

entities.name: Indian subcontinent exposure
entities.description: Travel, migration, or residence in India, Bangladesh, or Pakistan where amoebic infection prevalence is endemic.

entities.name: Sub-Saharan Africa travel
entities.description: Exposure to high parasite burden and poor municipal sanitation in rural or peri-urban sub-Saharan African regions.

entities.name: Mesoamerica and Mexico travel
entities.description: Travel or residence in Mexico and Central America, regions with well-documented high incidence of amoebic liver abscess.

entities.name: Oral-anal sexual contact
entities.description: Direct sexual oro-anal intercourse (anilingus) facilitating direct transmission of infectious cyst forms.

entities.name: Institutional crowding
entities.description: Residence in psychiatric facilities, prisons, or crowded long-term care homes with shared sanitary infrastructure.

entities.name: Daycare center exposure
entities.description: Close contact with diapered infants and contaminated diaper-changing surfaces in preschool childcare facilities.

entities.name: Household carrier contact
entities.description: Living in the same domicile as an asymptomatic chronic cyst shedder or infected food handler.

entities.name: Adult male sex
entities.description: Men aged 20 to 50 years who have a 7- to 10-fold higher susceptibility to amoebic liver abscess than females.

entities.name: Chronic alcohol misuse
entities.description: Heavy alcohol consumption acting as a major cofactor for hepatic abscess through immune suppression and iron stores.

entities.name: Hepatic iron overload
entities.description: Elevated hepatic parenchymal iron content providing essential nutritional cofactor for amoebic proliferation.

entities.name: MSM sexual activity
entities.description: Demographic group with elevated rates of sexually acquired intestinal and hepatic amebiasis in non-endemic countries.

entities.name: Systemic corticosteroid therapy
entities.description: Iatrogenic immunosuppression with steroids precipitating catastrophic fulminant necrotizing colitis or toxic megacolon.

entities.name: Malnutrition and poverty
entities.description: Protein-calorie malnutrition and impoverished living conditions compromising gut barrier mucosal defenses.

entities.name: Pregnancy and postpartum state
entities.description: Pregnant women, particularly in the third trimester, at heightened risk for aggressive fulminant colitis.

entities.name: Extremes of age
entities.description: Infants, young children, and elderly patients who face substantially higher case-fatality rates from invasive colitis.

entities.name: Two-to-four-week incubation
entities.description: Standard clinical incubation period from cyst ingestion to initial symptoms of colitis or liver abscess.

entities.name: Several month incubation lag
entities.description: Extended incubation interval observed in travelers presenting with liver abscess months after leaving endemic zones.

entities.name: Multi-year incubation latency
entities.description: Rare prolonged latency where asymptomatic intestinal cyst colonization persists for years prior to invasive hepatic spread.

entities.name: Marked peripheral eosinophilia
entities.description: Absolute eosinophil count >1,000/mcL or >10% of total white blood cells, characteristic of invasive helminths.

entities.name: Foul putrid abscess odor
entities.description: Malodorous, feculent, or foul odor of aspirated fluid caused by anaerobic bacteria in pyogenic liver abscess.

entities.name: Negative post-day-7 serology
entities.description: Non-reactive anti-amoebic IgG antibodies in serum collected beyond one week after hepatic symptom onset.

entities.name: Calcified hepatic cyst wall
entities.description: Thick, curvilinear, calcified fibrous wall encircling a liver lesion, pathognomonic of Echinococcus granulosus.

entities.name: Multiple internal daughter vesicles
entities.description: Honeycomb internal architecture and daughter cysts within a main cyst cavity typical of echinococcal infection.

entities.name: Water-lily sign
entities.description: Floating, collapsed, undulating parasitic endocyst membranes visible within a liver fluid cavity.

entities.name: Hyperacute fever with tenesmus
entities.description: Sudden explosive illness onset within 24 hours with temperature >39.5°C and prostration typical of shigellosis.

entities.name: Sheets of fecal neutrophils
entities.description: Dense confluent sheets of intact polymorphonuclear neutrophils covering the fecal microscopic smear.

entities.name: Gram stain positive aspirate
entities.description: Visualization of bacterial Gram-negative bacilli or Gram-positive cocci on direct microscopic examination of aspirate.

entities.name: Positive bacterial blood culture
entities.description: Isolation of enteric pathogens (e.g., Klebsiella pneumoniae, E. coli) from blood culture bottles.

entities.name: Skip lesions with granulomas
entities.description: Discontinuous colonic transmural inflammatory lesions containing non-caseating granulomas on histopathology.

entities.name: Continuous mucosal pseudopolyps
entities.description: Uninterrupted circumferential superficial mucosal ulceration and pseudopolyps extending proximally from the rectum.

entities.name: Histopathologic malignant dysplasia
entities.description: Identification of neoplastic dysplastic glandular epithelium on endoscopic biopsy of a cecal mass lesion.

entities.name: Persistent ameboma after metronidazole
entities.description: Failure of a colonic mass lesion to diminish or resolve on imaging after four weeks of nitroimidazole therapy.

entities.name: Fever past 72 hours
entities.description: Lack of defervescence or clinical symptom improvement within 72 hours of starting therapeutic doses of metronidazole.

entities.name: Bilobar multiple microabscesses
entities.description: Presence of numerous tiny (<1 cm) microabscesses widely scattered across both liver lobes on CT imaging.

entities.name: Presence of biliary stones
entities.description: Ultrasound demonstration of choledocholithiasis or acute ascending cholangitis with common bile duct dilatation.

entities.name: Non-pathogenic Entamoeba PCR
entities.description: Molecular PCR assay detecting exclusively Entamoeba dispar, moshkovskii, or bangladeshi without E. histolytica.

entities.name: Green bilious abscess pus
entities.description: Bright green or heavily bile-stained purulent material aspirated from a hepatic cavity.

entities.name: High procalcitonin elevation
entities.description: Marked elevation of serum procalcitonin (>5 to 10 ng/mL) accompanying septic shock.

entities.name: Normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate
entities.description: Completely normal ESR and normal CRP levels in an acute febrile patient with a hepatic mass lesion.

entities.name: Spontaneous non-antimicrobial resolution
entities.description: Complete spontaneous cessation of bloody diarrhea within 48 hours without antiparasitic treatment.

entities.name: Pyogenic liver abscess
entities.description: Bacterial hepatic infection occurring in older patients with biliary disease, yielding foul green pus on aspiration.

entities.name: Echinococcal hydatid cyst
entities.description: Slow-growing parasitic cyst caused by Echinococcus granulosus characterized by thick calcified wall, daughter vesicles, and eosinophilia.

entities.name: Bacillary dysentery
entities.description: Acute colitis caused by Shigella or Campylobacter characterized by hyperacute onset, high fever (>39°C), and sheets of fecal neutrophils.

entities.name: Ulcerative colitis
entities.description: Idiopathic inflammatory bowel disease presenting with continuous, symmetric mucosal inflammation and friability extending from rectum.

entities.name: Crohn disease
entities.description: Transmural granulomatous enteritis exhibiting cobblestoning, skip lesions, fistulas, and non-caseating granulomas.

entities.name: Colorectal carcinoma
entities.description: Malignant neoplasm of the colon presenting with right lower quadrant mass, weight loss, and dysplastic malignant cytology.

entities.name: Entamoeba dispar colonization
entities.description: Non-pathogenic commensal protozoan colonization morphologically identical to E. histolytica but lacking tissue invasiveness.

entities.name: Campylobacter enteritis
entities.description: Acute bacterial enterocolitis presenting with severe crampy abdominal pain, fever, and acute watery to bloody diarrhea.

entities.name: Salmonella enterica enteritis
entities.description: Foodborne bacterial infection causing acute fever, abdominal pain, nausea, and watery to bloody diarrhea.

entities.name: Acute appendicitis
entities.description: Acute bacterial inflammation and obstruction of the appendix causing focal RLQ peritonitis and requiring appendectomy.

entities.name: Biliary tract sepsis
entities.description: Ascending cholangitis and acute cholecystitis presenting with Charcot triad of fever, jaundice, and RUQ pain.

entities.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
entities.description: Primary hepatic malignancy arising in cirrhosis with alpha-fetoprotein elevation, arterial enhancement, and venous washout.

entities.name: Hepatic cystadenoma
entities.description: Benign multilocular cystic neoplasm of the biliary epithelium presenting as an afebrile septated liver mass.

entities.name: Cytomegalovirus colitis
entities.description: Opportunistic viral colitis in severely immunocompromised individuals characterized by intranuclear inclusion bodies.

entities.name: Clostridioides difficile colitis
entities.description: Toxin-mediated antibiotic-associated colitis characterized by mucosal pseudomembranes and positive fecal toxin assays.

entities.name: Schistosomiasis mansoni
entities.description: Chronic trematode infection causing Symmers pipestem periportal fibrosis, portal hypertension, and marked eosinophilia.

entities.name: Fascioliasis
entities.description: Zoonotic hepatic fluke infection presenting with marked peripheral eosinophilia, fever, and branching migratory tracks on liver CT.

entities.name: Tuberculous peritonitis
entities.description: Mycobacterial peritoneal infection presenting with high protein exudative ascites and elevated adenosine deaminase.

relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Invasive colonic disease manifesting with frequent bloody, mucoid evacuations, abdominal cramping, and rectal tenesmus.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Subacute amoebic colitis manifests with dark red altered bloody mucoid bowel movements resembling currant jelly.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Intestinal amoebic infection typically presents with gradual, worsening crampy lower abdominal pain over several weeks.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Severe rectal inflammation and ulceration cause persistent, agonizing tenesmus during active amoebic dysentery.
[MANIFESTS_AS] The majority of symptomatic intestinal amebiasis cases manifest as uncomplicated colitis without systemic toxic collapse.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Uncomplicated amoebic dysentery characteristically presents without high fever in up to 80% of patients.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Amebiasis can progress into fulminant necrotizing colitis with extensive transmural gangrene and high mortality.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Severe amoebic inflammation can precipitate toxic megacolon, especially when misdiagnosed as inflammatory bowel disease and treated with corticosteroids.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Deep flask-shaped mucosal ulcerations eroding through the muscularis propria can cause free or contained colonic perforation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Chronic localised amebiasis manifests as an amoeboma, an inflammatory pseudotumoral mass of the cecum or ascending colon mimicking adenocarcinoma.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Post-inflammatory cicatricial healing following invasive amebic colitis can result in focal, obstructing colonic strictures.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Persistent low-grade Entamoeba infection manifests as chronic colitis with waxing and waning diarrhea, weight loss, and asthenia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Invasive trophozoite erosion into colonic submucosal blood vessels can provoke acute, life-threatening lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Amebic mucosal invasion may localize to the appendix, producing appendiceal amebiasis with localized right lower quadrant peritonitis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Hematogenous portal vein migration of trophozoites manifests as amoebic liver abscess with sterile liquefactive parenchymal necrosis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Amoebic hepatic parenchymal necrosis stretches Glisson capsule, manifesting as persistent right upper quadrant ache.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute amoebic liver abscess typically presents with remittent high fever reaching 38.5°C to 40.0°C within one to two weeks.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Extraintestinal hepatic amebiasis frequently manifests with drenching diaphoresis and nocturnal pyrexial swings.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Amebiasis manifesting as liver abscess paradoxically lacks concurrent diarrhea or gastrointestinal symptoms in 70% to 80% of patients.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Liver abscess expansion produces palpable, tender hepatomegaly with exquisite discomfort upon hepatic palpation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Amebic liver abscess abutting the diaphragmatic dome irritates phrenic nerve sensory fibers, manifesting as referred right shoulder pain.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Sustained cytokine release and tissue necrosis in subacute amoebic liver abscess manifest as marked weight loss and profound anorexia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Large or rapidly expanding amoebic hepatic cavities can undergo amoebic liver rupture into surrounding serous cavities.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Rupture of an amoebic hepatic abscess into the peritoneal cavity produces severe chemical and inflammatory amoebic peritonitis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Superior extension of amoebic liver abscess manifests as pleuropulmonary amebiasis with basilar pulmonary consolidation and effusion.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Subdiaphragmatic inflammation induces transdiaphragmatic capillary leak, manifesting as a sterile sympathetic pleural effusion.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Transdiaphragmatic rupture of a superior hepatic abscess into the right pleural space manifests as massive amoebic empyema.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Erosion of an amoebic liver abscess through the diaphragm into pulmonary parenchyma creates a direct hepatobronchial fistula.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Formation of a hepatobronchial fistula manifests with dramatic expectoration of copious reddish-brown anchovy-paste sputum.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Diaphragmatic elevation and contiguous inflammatory spread manifest as right lower lobe consolidation and atelectasis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Contiguous extension or direct rupture of a left lobe amoebic liver abscess into the pericardium manifests as acute amoebic pericarditis.

[RULED_OUT_BY] Amoebic liver abscess is ruled out by marked peripheral eosinophilia (>1000/mcL or >10%), which points to helminthic etiology.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated amoebic abscess is ruled out by foul putrid abscess odor, which establishes bacterial pyogenic abscess.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Amoebic liver abscess is effectively ruled out by negative post-day-7 serology, as IgG sensitivity exceeds 95% after one week.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Amebic liquefactive necrosis is ruled out by a calcified hepatic cyst wall on ultrasound or CT, diagnostic of hydatid cyst.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Amoebic liver abscess is ruled out by multiple internal daughter vesicles on imaging, establishing hydatid disease.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Amoebic cavity is ruled out by the water-lily sign on sonography, which represents detached echinococcal endocyst membranes.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Subacute amoebic colitis is ruled out by hyperacute fever with tenesmus developing within 24 hours, favoring bacillary dysentery.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Pure amoebic dysentery is ruled out by sheets of fecal neutrophils on smear, which indicates bacterial bacillary dysentery.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated amoebic abscess is ruled out by a Gram stain positive aspirate showing bacterial pathogens.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess is ruled out by a positive bacterial blood culture indicating pyogenic liver abscess.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Amoebic colitis is ruled out by skip lesions with granulomas on endoscopic biopsy, establishing Crohn disease.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Discrete amebic ulceration is ruled out by continuous mucosal pseudopolyps and absence of normal intervening mucosa.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Inflammatory amoeboma is ruled out by histopathologic malignant dysplasia, which establishes colonic adenocarcinoma.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Benign amoeboma is ruled out by persistent ameboma after metronidazole therapy, demanding surgical resection for malignancy.

[RULED_OUT_BY] Amoebic liver abscess is ruled out by bilobar multiple microabscesses, which strongly indicates pylephlebitis, sepsis, or candidiasis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Pure amoebic liver abscess is ruled out by the presence of biliary stones and cholangitis as the primary source of hepatic suppuration.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Invasive amebiasis is ruled out by non-pathogenic Entamoeba PCR confirming commensal colonization rather than E. histolytica.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated amoebic abscess is ruled out by green bilious abscess pus, which confirms a communication with the biliary tree.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Isolated uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess is ruled out by high procalcitonin elevation, which indicates bacterial septicemia.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Acute invasive amoebic abscess is ruled out by a normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate and normal CRP at presentation.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Invasive amoebic colitis is ruled out by spontaneous non-antimicrobial resolution within 48 hours, favoring transient viral gastroenteritis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from pyogenic liver abscess, which affects older diabetics with biliary stones, is often multiple, yields foul bacterial pus, and requires prolonged antibacterials.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from echinococcal hydatid cyst, which is afebrile, features calcified laminated walls and daughter vesicles on imaging, and displays peripheral eosinophilia.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from bacillary dysentery, which presents hyperacutely with high fever, intense toxemia, and dense sheets of stool neutrophils.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from ulcerative colitis, which displays continuous mucosal involvement from rectum proximally without normal intervening mucosa, whereas amebiasis shows discrete ulcers.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Crohn disease, which exhibits transmural granulomas, cobblestoning, and fistulizing tract formation on biopsy rather than amoebic trophozoite invasion.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from colorectal carcinoma, as a cecal amoeboma presents as a malignant-appearing mass that completely resolves after 4 weeks of metronidazole.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Entamoeba dispar colonization, which lacks erythrophagocytosis, does not invade intestinal mucosa, produces no seroconversion, and requires no treatment.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Campylobacter enteritis, which has an acute 2- to 5-day foodborne incubation, high fever, and positive bacterial stool culture.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Salmonella enterica enteritis, which presents hyperacutely with prominent nausea, early vomiting, fever, and positive bacterial cultures.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from acute appendicitis, as amebic appendicitis occurs in the setting of dysenteric colitis and resolves with medical amebicides.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from biliary tract sepsis, which presents with marked hyperbilirubinemia, biliary ductal dilation, and positive bacterial blood cultures.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from hepatocellular carcinoma, which occurs with chronic cirrhosis, elevated alpha-fetoprotein, and solid hypervascular dynamic enhancement on CT.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from hepatic cystadenoma, which is an indolent, afebrile, multiseptated cystic neoplasm occurring in middle-aged women without inflammatory response.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from cytomegalovirus colitis, which occurs in advanced HIV or post-transplant immunosuppression with endothelial viral inclusions on biopsy.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Clostridioides difficile colitis, which follows recent antibacterial therapy, exhibits adherent yellow mucosal pseudomembranes, and tests positive for toxins A/B.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Schistosomiasis mansoni, which presents with periportal pipestem fibrosis, splenomegaly, and high eosinophilia rather than a focal liquefactive abscess.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from fascioliasis, which features profound eosinophilia (>1,000/mcL), history of watercress consumption, and branching tunnel tracks on liver imaging.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from tuberculous peritonitis, which is chronic, presents with high adenosine deaminase in ascitic fluid, and lacks anchovy-paste necrotic fluid.
